region.text: Sindh, ruled by the Talpur Mirs from Hyderabad

ledger.note: 1783: Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur defeats the Kalhoras at Halani and declares himself Rais of Sindh. The page: the dynasty was 'established by Mir Fateh Ali Khan in 1783'; he defeated the Kalhoras at the Battle of Halani in 1783 and declared himself Rais, or ruler, of Sindh, and Sindh was divided into semi-autonomous states (Hyderabad, Khairpur, Mirpur Khas, Tando Muhammad Khan). The History of Sindh page: the Talpurs 'succeeded the Kalhoras in 1783'. No month on the pages. For most of their rule they 'were subordinate or subject to the Durrani Empire and paid tribute to them' (undated; the Durrani dossier records the vassalage).

1839: the British take Karachi. The page: 'The British conquered Karachi in 1839, aided by Khojas and Hindus, and then pressed on Hyderabad, forcing tribute.' Month from the Karachi page (reviewer sa-05-g): 'The British East India Company captured Karachi on 3 February 1839 after HMS Wellesley opened fire and quickly destroyed Manora Fort'. The British conquest page also has the Royal Navy capturing 'the strategic outpost and Karachi' (undated). The rest of Sindh follows in 1843. The extent of 'Karachi' is a 30 km disc, the reader's reading of the town.

region.text: Matiari, Miani, Hyderabad and Dubba, where Napier fought the Amirs from 16 February to 24 March 1843

ledger.note: 17 February 1843: Napier defeats the Talpur Amirs at Miani. 'The battle took place on 17 February 1843 at Miani, Sindh'; on 16 February Napier 'arrived at Matiari from Hala'. The British conquest page's infobox runs the war 17 February-24 March 1843. The zone is the Hyderabad district of the campaign, a 60 km disc round Hyderabad; the pages name Matiari, Miani, Hyderabad and Dubba and no other ground.

region.text: Matiari, Miani, Hyderabad and Dubba, where Napier fought the Amirs from 16 February to 24 March 1843

ledger.note: 24 March 1843: the last Talpur army is beaten at Dubba. The page: 'defeat of Mir Sher Muhammad Talpur on 24 March 1843 at the battleground of Dubbo', after which Sindh was annexed. The Miani page has Sher Muhammad reaching Hyderabad on 24 March with about 8,000 men and being 'defeated in the Battle of Dubba'.

region.text: Sindh except the Khairpur branch's state, annexed after Miani and Dubba

ledger.note: 1843: the British annex Sindh to the Bombay Presidency. The British conquest page's infobox result: 'Annexation of Sindh into the Bombay Presidency within British India'; the Talpur page: Sindh was annexed 'to British India under the East India Company'. Neither page dates the annexation (Khairpur is left out here, see the next event); month 3 is the date of the last battle.

region.text: the Khairpur branch of the Talpurs in upper Sindh, kept by Mir Ali Murad

ledger.note: 1843: Khairpur survives as a princely state under British protection. The Talpur infobox: Khairpur 'continued in upper Sindh as the Khairpur princely state until 1955: 1843'; the Battle of Miani page: Napier 'had already secured the cooperation of the Amir of Khairpur, Mir Ali Murad Talpur, through promises of land and titles'. The area is the Khairpur page's 15,730 km2 (no year), drawn as a 70 km disc; the Talpur page says Ali Murad was later accused of plotting and lost lands in upper Sindh (undated). A British treaty of 1832 had already recognised Khairpur as independent (Talpur page; see notes).

1843: the Talpur state of Sindh ends. Infobox end date 1843; Hyderabad Talpurs 'defeated by the British at the Battle of Miani on 17 February 1843', Sher Muhammad defeated on 24 March 1843. Month 3 is the last battle; the pages give no date for the annexation. The Hyderabad Mirs were exiled to the Andaman Islands (Miani page).

wars.name: Shah Shuja's invasion of Sindh
wars.outcome: The Talpur brothers united and defeated him. The page: 'In 1832, Afghan king Shah Shuja invaded Sindh', and the brothers united to defeat him.
wars.note: The page gives no battle, no place and no ground lost, so no contest event is recorded; the year is the page's.

wars.name: British capture of Karachi
wars.outcome: The British held Karachi from 1839 and pressed on Hyderabad, forcing tribute.
wars.note: 'The British conquered Karachi in 1839, aided by Khojas and Hindus.' The Talpur page does not mention the First Anglo-Afghan War.

wars.name: British conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: British victory at Miani (17 February 1843) and Hyderabad/Dubba (24 March 1843); Sindh annexed to the Bombay Presidency; Khairpur, whose Amir Napier had won over, survived as a princely state.
wars.note: Infobox: 17 February 1843 - 24 March 1843. Before the war the Amirs signed 'a treaty of friendship' in 1809 and, in 1838, a political residency treaty admitting a British resident to Hyderabad, followed by British troops stationed 'for the protection of the Amirs' at their cost (undated).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line, a survey or a boundary for the Talpur lands. The Sindh province is a modern outline used for the state; the Khairpur disc is approximate and the eastern frontier in the Thar desert is unverified.

notes:
Talpur dynasty (Cliopatria 'Talpur Dynasty' 1820-1894, 15 shapes). Nine pages opened, one of them by mistake (Conquest_of_Sindh is the 711 conquest), so eight were useful. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Sindh returned url_not_found.

Main findings. (1) The state is the Talpur Mirs of Sindh, 1783-1843, not 1820-1894. Cliopatria's row starts 37 years late and ends 1894, the year Ali Murad of Khairpur died. This dossier covers 1783-1843 and adds a 1783-1819 keyframe. (2) Fourteen of the fifteen Cliopatria shapes are wrong or adjusted. 1822-1839 (535,464 and 528,678 km2) are Sindh plus all of Balochistan, five times the infobox 'over 100,000 square kilometers' and close to Kalat's 1835 area of 560,000 km2; 1840-41 and 1846-1894 are Gilgit-Baltistan outlines (Dogra conquest of Skardu by 1840, Gilgit Agency 1888-89), unrelated to Sindh; 1842-45 is Sindh plus Gilgit-Baltistan. 1820 is the only near-right shape (Sindh with strips of Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat and without a third of Sindh). Whoever owns Kashmir/Gilgit (sa-06, kashmir-and-jammu) or Kalat (khanate-of-kalat) should check whether those Cliopatria areas were meant for them; the 1840 start matches the Dogra conquest of Baltistan. (3) After 1843 the only Talpur land is Khairpur, which this dossier hands to the successor 'khairpur-state' (15,730 km2 on its page; here a 70 km disc). A dossier for it is needed; the 1843 'split' event and the successor entry point at it.

Not settled. The Talpur page says 'In 1832 ... Ali Murad secured recognition as the independent ruler of Khairpur' in a British treaty; the Khairpur page names Rustam Ali Khan as ruler 1830-1842 and Ali Murad from 1842, so the page's ruler is anachronistic. Khairpur is kept inside this state until 1843 because the Talpur page calls the four branches semi-autonomous states of one dynasty; a Khairpur dossier may start it in 1832 instead. The Durrani tribute (page: 'for most of their rule') is undated on the pages opened; the Durrani dossier already records 1783 vassal_start and 1818 vassal_end for this slug. The British 1838 residency treaty (a protectorate in all but name) is dated by the British conquest page; british-empire already records a 1838 vassal_start for this slug; no event of it is recorded here because a vassal event belongs to the suzerain. The 1839 loss of Karachi has no mirror gain in british-empire or east-india-company; they should add it (page: Talpur dynasty, 'The British conquered Karachi in 1839'). The pages are silent on Shikarpur, Sukkur, Rohri, Umerkot, Bahawalpur, Multan and Sikh frontier claims, so no event rests on them. The Talpur page's Mirpur Khas branch (Sher Muhammad, 'until 1843') and the Tando Muhammad Khan branch have no separate land on any page. The rulers are the Hyderabad branch only; the page's years differ by one in two places (1801/1802, 1832/1833). Month of the annexation: neither page dates it; 24 March 1843 is the last battle.

Sind admin1 (gazetteer 'Sind', Pakistan, 562 cells, 142,130 km2) is the working outline of Talpur land; the Talpur infobox 'over 100,000 square kilometers' (no year) fits. Gazetteer names: Sind, Khairpur, Karachi, Hyderabad (Pakistan) all resolve.
